investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract evidence gap.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable state. Because no VM is provisioned, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completes, and the probe exits without writing any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an infrastructure capacity constraint localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or a change to the eval contracts. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is currently confirmed only at the eval layer.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — the scheduler explicitly names kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion as the blocking condition.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message with pod stuck for 143s, confirming the condition persisted across a second independent probe attempt.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message with pod stuck for 148s, confirming the condition persisted across a third independent probe attempt.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe never reaching the VM-provisioning step.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), confirming the runner returned before writing any evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; a scheduling failure upstream of this call would prevent any evidence from being written.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=140836 (~134s wall time) matches the scheduler's reported 'pod stuck unscheduled for 134s', confirming the probe timed out waiting for the pod to become schedulable.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187: remote-agent-create is marked required=true with outageLatencyMs=360000; the check failed well within that window, meaning the failure is due to the pod never scheduling rather than a latency threshold breach.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote agent VMs or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector rules, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible for remote agent pods. If those 2 nodes lose capacity, the entire feature becomes unschedulable. This is a contributing constraint amplifying the capacity problem.

Tertiary — resource leak or stuck VMs: previously provisioned remote agent VMs may not have been cleaned up (e.g., failed cleanup in withCleanup at run-status-probes.mjs line 1883), holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new allocations. This is plausible but unconfirmed without cluster state evidence.

Lower confidence — node count insufficient for the workload: the cluster has only 6 nodes total, with only 2 carrying the required resource type. A cluster scaling or node provisioning failure could have reduced available capacity below the minimum needed.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-29T21:53–21:58Z with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes have only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that every attempt to schedule a peer-pod VM for a remote agent failed before the agent could be created. Because agent creation is a prerequisite for state polling (the runner calls createAgent at run-status-probes.mjs:1905 before any state evidence can be collected), the remote-agent-state check never reached the polling stage and produced zero evidence, causing the full contract gap (orgId, agentId, readyState, state). This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector, meaning all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads or leaked pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: only 2 nodes are configured to host kata peer-pod VMs; the other 4 are ineligible by label or taint, reducing effective capacity to those 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any resource pressure.

Tertiary — leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from prior eval runs consuming VM slots: if previous eval cleanup (withCleanup at run-status-probes.mjs:1903) did not fully terminate peer-pod VMs, those slots would remain occupied and prevent new scheduling.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the cluster's kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes showed available (unallocated) VM slots at the time of the eval run, resource exhaustion would not be the cause and a different scheduling or API failure would need to be investigated.

If the remote-agent-create sibling check had passed (i.e., an agent was successfully created) while remote-agent-state failed, the root cause would be localized to the state-polling API rather than VM scheduling.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure window succeeded without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient scheduling race rather than sustained resource exhaustion.

If the scheduler message were absent from the check message and the evidence object contained partial keys (e.g., orgId and agentId present but readyState missing), the failure would point to a state-polling API defect rather than a scheduling failure.
If only remote-agent-state failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-runtime passed, the diagnosis would shift to a state-polling-specific regression rather than a shared VM capacity problem.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, so capacity exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure check rather than a scheduling timeout buried in an agent-creation eval.
Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no kata.peerpods.io/vm pods from prior eval runs remain in Running or Pending state after the withCleanup phase completes.
Add a node-affinity coverage eval that asserts the number of nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm label meets a minimum threshold, catching configuration drift that reduces the eligible node pool.

Consider adding a dedicated remote-agents capacity check to infra/evals/status/features.json that polls VM slot availability independently of agent creation, enabling earlier warning before all slots are consumed.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract evidence gap.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. With 0/6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable state. Because no VM is provisioned, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completes, and the probe exits without writing any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an infrastructure capacity constraint localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or a change to the eval contracts. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is currently confirmed only at the eval layer.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — the scheduler explicitly names kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion as the blocking condition.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message with pod stuck for 143s, confirming the condition persisted across a second independent probe attempt.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message with pod stuck for 148s, confirming the condition persisted across a third independent probe attempt.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe never reaching the VM-provisioning step.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), confirming the runner returned before writing any evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; a scheduling failure upstream of this call would prevent any evidence from being written.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=140836 (~134s wall time) matches the scheduler's reported 'pod stuck unscheduled for 134s', confirming the probe timed out waiting for the pod to become schedulable.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187: remote-agent-create is marked required=true with outageLatencyMs=360000; the check failed well within that window, meaning the failure is due to the pod never scheduling rather than a latency threshold breach.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote agent VMs or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector rules, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible for remote agent pods. If those 2 nodes lose capacity, the entire feature becomes unschedulable. This is a contributing constraint amplifying the capacity problem.

Tertiary — resource leak or stuck VMs: previously provisioned remote agent VMs may not have been cleaned up (e.g., failed cleanup in withCleanup at run-status-probes.mjs line 1883), holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new allocations. This is plausible but unconfirmed without cluster state evidence.

Lower confidence — node count insufficient for the workload: the cluster has only 6 nodes total, with only 2 carrying the required resource type. A cluster scaling or node provisioning failure could have reduced available capacity below the minimum needed.

Because no pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.

If the scheduler message were absent from the check message and the evidence object contained partial keys (e.g., orgId and agentId present but readyState missing), the failure would point to a state-polling API defect rather than a scheduling failure.
If only remote-agent-state failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-runtime passed, the diagnosis would shift to a state-polling-specific regression rather than a shared VM capacity problem.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted by the eval runner was stuck unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No remote agent VM was ever provisioned, so the eval never reached the point of collecting any evidence, and all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the two eligible nodes. Only 2 of 6 nodes are configured to supply this resource, and both reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" at scheduling time. The remaining 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, and preemption found no victims to evict. Because no VM pod could be scheduled, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs never returned a live agent, the eval timed out after ~148 s, and zero evidence was collected. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real capacity constraint in the production Kubernetes cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs consumed all available VM slots and none were released before this eval run, leaving 0 schedulable capacity.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-kata nodes may have had their labels changed or the pod spec's affinity rules may be overly restrictive, reducing the eligible node pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall.

Tertiary — VM pod leak from a prior eval run: if a previous createAgent() call was not cleaned up (e.g., withCleanup() did not fire due to an earlier crash), leaked VM pods could be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, preventing new scheduling.

Lower confidence — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: all three sibling checks ran within a ~5-minute window (remote-agent-create ended 21:53, remote-agent-state ended 21:55, remote-agent-runtime ended 21:58), suggesting simultaneous VM requests that together exceeded the 2-node capacity.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the two kata-capable nodes immediately using kubectl to determine current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity and whether any pods are holding slots from prior eval runs or other workloads.

Determine whether the 4 nodes excluded by node affinity/selector are intentionally excluded (security/isolation requirement) or whether their labels have drifted; if drift, restore the correct labels to expand the schedulable pool.

Evaluate whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the two eligible nodes is sufficient for the expected concurrent eval load (3 sibling checks running within a 5-minute window each requiring a VM pod); if not, request additional node capacity or stagger the eval schedule.

Consider adding a pre-flight capacity check to the eval runner that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm availability before attempting createAgent() for remote agents, and surfaces a more actionable SKIP or WARN status when capacity is zero rather than waiting for the full scheduling timeout.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the two kata-capable nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity available and not exhausted at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling policy or quota issue should be investigated.

If the pod spec's node affinity/selector is found to be intentionally excluding the 4 non-kata nodes for a valid reason (e.g., security isolation), and the 2 kata nodes have sufficient capacity, then the root cause would shift to a transient spike in concurrent VM demand rather than sustained exhaustion.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and collects all 5 required evidence fields, it would indicate a transient capacity spike rather than a persistent exhaustion or misconfiguration.

If no prior eval run pods are found holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (ruling out leaks), and capacity is confirmed available, the cause would shift to a race condition or quota enforcement issue rather than resource exhaustion.

If the local-agent-runtime sibling check (which uses the same evidence contract shape but a different agent type) is also failing at the same time, it would suggest a broader API or auth failure rather than a kata VM scheduling issue.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all nodes and fails with a WARN if available slots fall below a minimum threshold (e.g., 1), providing early warning before agent creation is attempted.

Add a VM pod leak detection eval that lists all pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources older than a configurable TTL (e.g., 10 minutes) and flags any that were not cleaned up by the eval runner's withCleanup() mechanism.
Add a node affinity/selector health eval that verifies the expected number of nodes match the remote agent pod's affinity rules, alerting if the schedulable pool drops below the expected count.

Consider staggering the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime eval checks so they do not all request VM pods within the same scheduling window, reducing peak concurrent demand on the two kata-capable nodes.
